questions.question: Fatty change (steatosis) of the liver is most commonly caused by:
questions.explanation: Also obesity, diabetes and malnutrition; reversible in early stages.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which pigment gives the ‘wear and tear’ brown atrophy appearance to the heart in elderly people?
questions.explanation: Perl's stain is positive for haemosiderin.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Amyloid is characteristically demonstrated by:

options.A: Congo red stain showing apple-green birefringence under polarised light

questions.explanation: It is a beta-pleated sheet protein deposited extracellularly.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Dystrophic calcification occurs in:

options.A: Dead or degenerating tissue with normal serum calcium

questions.explanation: Metastatic calcification occurs in normal tissue with hypercalcaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Squamous metaplasia of the bronchial epithelium is typically caused by:
questions.explanation: A reversible change; may progress to dysplasia and carcinoma.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An increase in the SIZE of cells leading to an increase in organ size is called:
questions.explanation: Hyperplasia is an increase in cell number; e.g. the pregnant uterus shows both.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The hallmark of chronic inflammation is infiltration by:

options.B: Mononuclear cells (macrophages, lymphocytes and plasma cells)

questions.explanation: Associated with fibrosis and tissue destruction.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Fibrinous inflammation is characteristically seen in:
questions.explanation: Resolves by organisation causing adhesions.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pus consists mainly of:

options.D: Dead neutrophils, tissue debris and bacteria

questions.explanation: A collection of pus in a cavity is an abscess.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which is an acute-phase reactant?
questions.explanation: ESR rises with fibrinogen elevation.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Granulation tissue consists of:

options.A: Proliferating capillaries, fibroblasts and inflammatory cells

questions.explanation: It appears red and granular in healing wounds.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which factor delays wound healing?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency impairs collagen formation.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Septic shock is characterised by:

options.D: Vasodilatation and reduced systemic vascular resistance caused by endotoxins

questions.explanation: Endotoxin (LPS) triggers the release of cytokines such as TNF and IL-1.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Lines of Zahn are characteristic of:

options.B: A fibrin clot in a test tube
options.C: A thrombus formed in flowing blood

questions.explanation: They are alternating pale (platelets/fibrin) and dark (red cell) layers.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Paradoxical embolism occurs through:

options.B: A patent foramen ovale or septal defect, passing from the venous to the arterial circulation

questions.explanation: Can cause stroke from a leg DVT.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Histological grading of a tumour refers to its degree of:
questions.explanation: Staging describes extent of spread (TNM).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A teratoma is a tumour that contains:

options.C: Tissues derived from all three germ layers

questions.explanation: Common in the ovary and testis.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Small cell lung carcinoma is commonly associated with a paraneoplastic secretion of:
questions.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma secretes PTHrP causing hypercalcaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Basal cell carcinoma of the skin is characterised by:

options.A: A rolled pearly edge with central ulceration (rodent ulcer), rarely metastasising

questions.explanation: Locally invasive; commonest skin cancer.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most important prognostic factor in cutaneous melanoma is:
questions.explanation: Measured in millimetres from the granular layer to the deepest invasion.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Burkitt's lymphoma is associated with:
questions.explanation: Starry-sky appearance on histology.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Class I HLA molecules (A, B, C) are present on:
questions.explanation: Present endogenous antigens to CD8 T cells.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Hyperacute graft rejection is caused by:
questions.explanation: Occurs within minutes to hours of transplantation.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Systemic anaphylaxis is a type of:
questions.explanation: Mediated by IgE-induced mast cell degranulation.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Bruton's agammaglobulinaemia is an X-linked disorder in which there is:

options.C: Absence of B cells and immunoglobulins

questions.explanation: Recurrent bacterial infections after 6 months of age.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which disease is inherited as autosomal dominant?
questions.explanation: Also Huntington's disease and familial hypercholesterolaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Haemophilia A is inherited as:
questions.explanation: Males are affected; females are carriers.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The karyotype in Klinefelter syndrome is:
questions.explanation: Tall stature, gynaecomastia and infertility.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The characteristic vascular lesion in malignant hypertension is:
questions.explanation: Rapid renal failure and papilloedema.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The earliest light-microscopic change of myocardial infarction (after 4–12 hours) is:
questions.explanation: Scar formation takes weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Cirrhosis is characterised by:

options.A: Diffuse fibrosis with regenerative nodules and disorganised architecture

questions.explanation: The commonest cause worldwide is chronic hepatitis B and alcohol.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A malignant gastric ulcer differs from a benign ulcer in having:

options.C: Rolled, everted margins and a necrotic base

questions.explanation: Biopsy of ulcer margins is mandatory.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Crescents on renal biopsy are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Proliferation of parietal epithelial cells in Bowman's space.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Kimmelstiel–Wilson nodules are seen in:
questions.explanation: Nodular glomerulosclerosis.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In rickets, the histological defect is:

options.D: Failure of mineralisation of osteoid and cartilage in growing bone

questions.explanation: Adult equivalent is osteomalacia.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The diagnostic feature of osteosarcoma on histology is:

options.C: Malignant osteoid production by tumour cells

questions.explanation: Codman's triangle and sunburst on X-ray.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Escherichia coli is a:
questions.explanation: The commonest cause of urinary tract infection.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which organism is a spore-forming obligate anaerobe?
questions.explanation: Bacillus anthracis is an aerobic spore-former.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Group A beta-haemolytic streptococcus is responsible for:
questions.explanation: ASO titre is raised after infection.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Mycoplasma pneumoniae differs from other bacteria in that it:
questions.explanation: Not affected by penicillins.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The causative organism of syphilis is:
questions.explanation: A painless chancre marks the primary stage.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Negri bodies are seen in the brain in:
questions.explanation: Eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Hepatitis C virus is transmitted mainly by:
questions.explanation: Commonly leads to chronic hepatitis.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Dengue virus is transmitted by:
questions.explanation: Day-biting mosquito.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Amoebic liver abscess is caused by:
questions.explanation: Anchovy sauce pus.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which helminth causes hookworm disease and iron-deficiency anaemia?
questions.explanation: Enters through the skin of bare feet.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: BCG is a:
questions.explanation: Tetanus vaccine is a toxoid; Salk polio vaccine is killed.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An antiseptic is a chemical used to:
questions.explanation: Disinfectants are for inanimate objects.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
